image_spec.headline: Only 17% of shoppers would cut back on the holiday meal.
image_spec.body: 46% would trim holiday clothing first. Where are you cutting back this year?
image_spec.tip: Some things stay on the table.

posts.caption:
Here's a number that made us smile. If money gets tight this season, only 17% of shoppers say they'd cut back on food for the holiday meal. Holiday clothing is the first thing to go, at 46%. That's from a new FMI and Hartman Group survey.

Makes sense to us. Nobody remembers the sweater. They remember who was at the table and whether there was enough stuffing. 🍗

So where are you trimming this year, and what's staying no matter what? Tell us in the comments.

#smartshopping #groceryshopping #familymeals #stashsmart #mobilepantry
posts.source_note: FMI (The Food Industry Association) and The Hartman Group, U.S. Grocery Shopper Trends 2026: Holidays (1,467 U.S. grocery shoppers, online, Sept 21 to 28, 2026): 17% would cut back on food for holiday meals if needed vs. 46% on holiday clothing and 45% on shows and events. https://massmarketretailers.com/fmi-research-holiday-shoppers-put-family-meals-first-lean-on-grocery-loyalty-programs-to-save/ (also The Shelby Report, Nov 13, 2026)

posts.caption:

On the Family plan in StashSmart, up to 4 people at home add to the same List. Your sister remembers the rolls. Your kid adds whipped cream. Twice. And before you grab the pumpkin, "Do I have this?" checks the pantry, so you don't come home to two cans. 🥫
